At the top of the Dashboard, four KPI tiles provide a high-level status overview for the

Completed Checklists (blue): Displays the total number of completed checklists.

Assigned Tasks (blue): Shows the total number of tasks assigned within the
selected period. This tile is informational and not clickable.
•
Positive / Negative Answers (green / red): Displays the total count of positive and
negative answers recorded in completed checklists. These values are informational

Tags
Tags are a way to categorize and filter markets according to custom criteria. They are
created at the company level and then assigned to individual markets and checklists. Each
tag belongs to a tag category, which serves as a grouping structure. While categories
organize tags logically, filtering is applied through the tags themselves. Once tags are
selected, the dashboard charts for checklists and tasks adjust dynamically according to
the chosen tag filters.
MCL supports three different types of tags:
•
Store / Store Group Tags – Used to categorize individual stores or defined store
groups. A store group can consist of one or multiple stores, depending on how the
structure is defined.
•
Checklist Group Tags – Used to group multiple checklists under a shared
classification. A checklist group can contain one or several checklists.
•
Individual Checklist Tags – Assigned to specific checklists for more granular
filtering and analysis.

The Batch Upload tab allows users to import or update multiple markets at once using an

ﬁle are deleted.
This feature saves time and ensures consistency when handling large market structures.

MCL Checklist Wizard – FAQ Guide

How do I access the Checklist Wizard in MCL?
To access the Checklist Wizard, open the Checklists tab from the main menu.
View, create, or manage existing checklists directly from this section.

How do I create a new checklist in MCL?
Click the + icon in the Checklist Wizard.
Enter a checklist name and complete all mandatory fields.
Set start and end dates, or choose a recurrence option (Daily, Weekly, etc.).
Select N/A if the checklist should always be available.
Review details, then click Save to confirm.

What fields are mandatory when creating a checklist?
Mandatory fields typically include:
Checklist name
Start and end dates (if applicable)
Department or role associations

How can I make a checklist always available?
Select N/A for start and end dates to keep the checklist active at all times.

How do I configure checklist recurrence or periodicity?
When setting up your checklist:
Choose a recurrence option under Scheduling (Daily, Weekly, or Custom).
Confirm that each recurrence period aligns with business needs.

How can I restrict or allow department selection for checklists?
In the configuration settings:
Enable or disable departments depending on where the checklist should appear.
Only departments you select will see the checklist in the MCL App.

During checklist setup, assign access under Roles.

Department selections determine checklist visibility across stores.

How do I select and organize questions within a checklist?

Choose questions by department.
Use the up/down arrows to reorder them.
Department order can also be adjusted later in the mobile app.
How can I send completed checklist reports to specific emails or
roles?
Use the Email Configuration tab to set up recipients.
Enter email addresses or link reports to roles such as Regional Manager.
This integrates with your company-wide or user-level email settings.

How do I preview a checklist before completing it?
Click Preview to review the checklist layout.
Once satisfied, select Complete to finalize and activate it.

How do I edit, delete, or export an existing checklist?
Use the icons beside your checklist name:

MCL Dashboard – FAQ Guide

What is displayed in the MCL Dashboard and how do I navigate it?
The MCL dashboard provides an overview of all operational areas, including checklists, questions, tasks,
reports, users, roles, departments, and markets.

How do I navigate the dashboard?
Navigation  is  done  from  the  side  menu,  allowing  you  to  switch  between  modules  and  monitor  key
performance indicators such as completed checklists or assigned tasks.

How do I create or edit a market in the dashboard?
To manage markets: - Go to the Markets section on the dashboard. - Click on the + icon to create a new
market, or click on the  Pencil Icon to edit an existing market. - Assign departments to each market to
ensure accurate data organization and transparency.

How do I add or edit departments in the dashboard?
Go to the Departments section to create or modify entries.
Click on the + icon to add new departments.
Define department names and link them to markets as needed.
Departments form the basis for assigning questions and checklists.

How do I create a new user in the system in the dashboard?
To add users: - Open the Users tab and click + to create a new profile.

In the dashboard, how do I manage a user in the system?
Assign credentials, a market, and a role.
Save the changes and check the permissions under Roles.

How do I assign roles and permissions to users in the dashboard?
Roles are configured under the Roles menu.
Select a role or create a role (e.g., Manager, Admin).
Customize permissions for each role, such as editing, viewing, or managing tasks, checklists, and
reports.
Assign roles to users in their profile settings.

How do I create questions by department in the dashboard?
Under Questions, you can create, edit, or filter questions. - Export questions to Excel for review if needed.

How do I filter questions by department in the dashboard?
Use department filters or keyword search to find items.
Each question must be linked to a department to appear in relevant checklists.

How do I create and edit checklists in the dashboard?
Open the Checklists section.
Click + to create a new checklist or click the Pencil Icon to change one.
Link checklists to specific departments and markets.
Add repeat, role, and visibility settings before saving.

How do I analyze checklist or question data in the dashboard?
Use the Data Analysis section. - Filter results by company, market, or time period. - Review key metrics such
as completion rates and response distributions. - Identify trends to improve performance and compliance.

How do I view assigned tasks in the dashboard?
Open the  Tasks module to view assigned items. - Click on a task to view details, add notes, or upload
photos.

How do I close assigned tasks in the dashboard?
Use the Close Task option if the issue is resolved.
Tasks can be assigned to users or markets to improve accountability.
How do I create a new task or announcement (newsletter) in the

dashboard?
From the dashboard, select Newsletters or Announcements. - Enter the title and message details. - Attach
optional photos or PDFs. - Ensure the sender is configured as a market contact to publish successfully.
How do I assign reports to specific roles and recipients in the

dashboard?
In the Assign Report Roles section: - Select a report and assign it to roles such as Manager or Admin. -
Add up to three email addresses for automatic delivery. - Save the settings for future reports.

Use the top navigation bar to switch between Checklists and Tasks. - Adjust the time period with filters
such as This Week, Last Week, Today, or Yesterday.

Which dashboard charts are interactive?
Charts such as Checklist Not Completed, Recurring Checklist Status, and Tasks by Status are interactive.
Clicking a bar or segment opens a detailed list of corresponding elements.
How do market and department assignments affect the visibility of

checklists?
A checklist appears only in stores where both the department and checklist settings match the assigned
markets. - If departments aren’t linked correctly, users won’t see the checklist.
What are the rules for creating, archiving, copying, and exporting

checklists in the dashboard?
From the Checklists menu, you can create, edit, delete, export, archive, or copy lists. - Archived checklists
can only be reactivated by the MCL team. - Copied checklists will appear as “Copy” until renamed. -
Checklists can be exported as Excel files.

How do I search, filter, and download checklist reports as PDFs?
Open the  Reports pane, use the search bar or filters to find a specific checklist, and download reports
directly as a PDF.
Where can I find monthly Excel exports for company-wide data in

the dashboard?
Monthly Excel exports are available under Exports & Company-wide Data. They include checklist and task
statuses, responses, and comments across all markets.

How do I analyze specific questions or answers in the dashboard?
Go to Data Analysis. - Filter by market, checklist, and time period. - View question-level answers and export
related PDF reports.

Who can edit or delete tasks in the dashboard and under what

conditions?
Only the task creator or a Company Administrator can edit a task if its status is Not Started. Completed or
in-progress tasks cannot be edited but can be deleted individually or in bulk.

How do I delete tasks in bulk in the dashboard?
In the Tasks section, use the checkbox selection tool to select multiple tasks, then click Delete Tasks.
When I create a task in the dashboard, how do I set photo or

comment requirements?
During task creation, enable options that require a photo or comment before completion. This ensures
additional context before closing a task.

How do I assign reports to specific roles in the dashboard?
In the  Checklist Edit View, open  Report Distribution. - Enable the role setting (“Yes”). - Select desired
markets, departments, or users. - Save the configuration for future checklists.
How do I create checklist groups in the dashboard and assign

checklists to them?
Under  Company → Groups, create groups and subgroups. - In the  Checklist Editor, assign checklists
under the Group field for easier filtering and navigation.

How can I include a new checklist in current dashboard analyses?
Enable  Include in Current Period when creating the checklist. This ensures it appears immediately in
dashboard data.

What can the MCL Dashboard do?
The MCL dashboard provides a centralized view of all checklists, tasks, and reports in stores. It allows
managers to track performance, close rates, and compliance metrics in real time.

What are the main functional areas of the MCL Dashboard?
Checklists: Displays active, completed, and overdue checklists.
Tasks: Shows task assignments, due dates, and progress.
Reports: Access completed checklist data and KPIs.

What color indicators are used in the dashboard charts?
Green: Completed items.

Total checklists created and completed.

Select a department or market from the drop-down menu or filters. - Charts update automatically to show
checklist performance and close rates.

What are recurring checklists and how are they tracked?
Recurring checklists are scheduled daily, weekly, or monthly. - Progress is shown in the  Status section,
highlighting due dates, completions, and open cycles.

What do you see in the Task Overview section of the dashboard?
Total open and completed tasks.
Distribution by priority and due date.
Automatic follow-ups triggered by negative checklist responses.
How do I analyze response quality and compliance trends in the

The analytics engine visualizes positive vs. negative responses, frequency of N/A, and photo/

This helps identify areas for improvement.

Export checklist, task, and report data to Excel or PDF.

What is the batch upload feature in the dashboard?
The batch upload feature allows administrators to upload multiple markets and users at once using Excel
templates.

How do I upload multiple markets at once in the dashboard?
Download the Excel template from the MCL web interface.
Fill in mandatory fields marked in red.
Upload via Market Upload option.
Assign departments and review configurations.

How do I upload multiple users at once in the dashboard?
Use the Excel template for user upload.
Fill in required fields (names, emails, roles).
Upload and link users to departments and markets.
Copy-pasting data will cause upload errors.

Which fields are required in upload templates?

What happens if there are errors while uploading?
Errors will appear in the Error Window. Review, correct in Excel, and re-upload.

Who can use the batch upload feature in the dashboard?
Only Enterprise Administrators have permission to perform batch uploads.

How can I check if uploaded data is active in the dashboard?
Check the Markets or Users overview. New entries appear immediately after validation.

What is the purpose of the tag function in the dashboard?
Tags categorize markets and checklists for easier grouping and filtering in dashboards and reports.

How do I create and configure tags in the dashboard?

What are tag categories in the dashboard and how are they used?
Tag categories organize tags structurally but cannot be used directly for filtering.

How do I assign tags to markets in the dashboard?
Open Markets, select a market, and go to Tags Tab. - Use checkboxes to assign tags.

Can tags be used to filter dashboard data?
Yes. Tags can filter checklists and tasks to enhance visibility and analytics.

Do tags affect KPI calculations in the dashboard?
No. Tags only filter data views and do not influence KPI results.

MCL Mobile & Web User Guide
Answers to common operational questions
Prepared 4 August 2026 | Product behavior may vary with company permissions and configuration.
This guide is written for store teams and administrators. Menu labels can differ slightly by language or app
version. Where a capability is controlled by permissions, ask your company MCL administrator if the option is
not visible.
Tasks and daily work

1. How do I create a task in the mobile app, step by step?
Creating tasks normally requires a role with task-creation permission.
1. Open Tasks from the app menu and tap the add/new-task button.
2. Enter a clear title and description; choose the due date and, if available, priority.
3. Select the store (market) and the coworker(s) who should complete it.
4. Attach evidence if needed, then save/send the task. The assignee sees it in their task list.

2. How do I fill out / complete a checklist in my store? What is the process?
Open the checklist scheduled for your store, select the relevant department if prompted, and answer every
required question. Use the response control configured for the question (for example Yes/No, number,
temperature, free text, or rating). Add comments or evidence when required. Review the progress indicator,
then tap Finish/Complete and confirm any signature requirement.

3. How do I start an inspection in a store? How do I run a routine inspection vs. a special one?
From the checklist or inspection area, select your store and the checklist. Choose Routine check for the
planned recurring inspection; select Special inspection for an ad-hoc inspection outside the routine schedule.
Complete the same question flow and finish the run. Special inspections are reported separately from routine
checks.
5. Open Checklists/Inspections.
6. Choose the market and checklist.
7. Choose Routine or Special when the app offers both options.
8. Complete, review and submit the inspection.

4. Can I attach a photo as evidence when I answer a checklist question? How?
Yes, when the question allows evidence. On the question, tap the camera/photo control, choose Camera or
Gallery, capture/select the image, confirm it, and then save the answer. Let the image upload during
synchronization before deleting it from the device.

5. Does MCL work offline? What happens if I lose internet in the middle of a checklist?
The mobile app keeps synchronized reference data and checklist work locally, so an in-progress checklist can
normally be continued without a connection. Uploads, refreshed data, final server submission, PDF
downloads, and some task actions require internet. Reconnect and synchronize before assuming the run is
visible to others.
Note: Do not clear app data or uninstall while offline: unsynchronized local work can be lost.
MCL User Guide | Internal training reference

6. How does sync work? How do I force the app to update if it shows old data?
MCL synchronizes the company data assigned to the logged-in user between the server and the device. To
refresh, first reconnect to the internet, return to the home screen or pull to refresh/reopen the app, and use the
available Sync/Update action if your version shows one. If the data remains old, sign out and back in only after
pending offline work has synchronized; then contact the administrator to verify your market, role, and checklist
assignments.

11. Do I get notifications or reminders when a task is due? How do I turn them on?
MCL can register the device for task notifications, but reminders depend on your company configuration. Allow
notifications for MCL in the phone operating-system settings and keep the app updated. If you do not receive
reminders, ask the administrator to check the task notification configuration and your assigned device/account.

12. What statuses can a task have (open, done, expired)? What happens when a task expires?
The task views distinguish open/pending work, completed work, and overdue/expired work. A task remains in
the overdue category after its due date until it is completed or otherwise handled under company policy; it
does not disappear automatically. Complete it with the requested evidence/comment and notify the task owner
if it needs reassignment or a new due date.

16. How do I assign a task to a coworker, and how do they mark it as done?
When creating or editing the task, select the target market and choose one or more users assigned to that
market; save the task. The coworker opens it from Tasks, completes the requested work, adds a
note/evidence if required, and uses the completion/close action. The task status then changes to completed.
22. As a normal store employee, what should I do every day in the app? What does a typical daily

routine look like?
A practical daily routine is:
9. Open MCL after connecting to the network and check whether today’s data has refreshed.
10. Review Tasks for due or overdue items.
11. Run the scheduled routine checklists for your store/department; record accurate answers and evidence at
the point of work.
12. Submit completed checklists and complete assigned tasks.
13. Before leaving, reconnect if necessary and confirm that the app has synchronized; resolve any failed
uploads or pending items.
Inspections, reports and dashboard

9. How do I see the results of my inspections? Are there reports somewhere?
In the mobile app, open Reports/Checklist History to view completed runs and their answers. On the web, use
Reports and Data Analysis/Dashboard for filtered, aggregated results. Available filters commonly include time
period, market group, checklist group and checklist; your role determines how much data you can see.

10. How do I open the dashboard on the web? What is the URL and what will I see there?
Open https://marktcheckliste.de/ in a browser and sign in with your MCL account. Your company may provide
a different branded or test URL; use that address if instructed. The dashboard shows filters and high-level
checklist/task cards (planned, open, completed and missed), completion/score charts, answer distributions
and trend analysis, according to your permissions.

present, ask the administrator to provide the report or enable the appropriate permission.

See the dashboard screenshot above. It contains a filter row, status cards, a trend chart, a response

Access, organization and configuration
7. What roles exist in MCL and what can each role do? What is the difference between a manager

and a normal user?
MCL uses company-defined roles and granular permissions, so role names can differ. A normal store user
generally runs assigned checklists, views permitted history and completes assigned tasks. A manager
normally has broader visibility across markets/departments and can review results, create/assign tasks, and
manage operational setup when those permissions are granted. Company administrators typically manage
users, roles, markets, departments, checklists and dashboard access.
Note: The definitive answer for an account is its assigned role permissions, not the job title alone.

8. What is a market in MCL? What is a department? How do they relate to my store?
A market is the MCL record for a store/location. A department is an operational area within that market, such
as produce, bakery, warehouse or checkout. Checklists and users can be assigned by market and
department, so a user sees the work relevant to the location and area they are responsible for.

13. How do I log in to the MCL app for the first time?
Install the MCL app supplied by your company, open it with an internet connection, enter the email/username
and password issued to you, and sign in. The app downloads your user profile and permitted market/checklist
data. Accept notification permission if you want task alerts. If authentication fails, confirm the account has
been created and assigned to a company/market.
[Figure mcl-user-guide-qa-en_p4_i1: The Tasks list in the MCL app.]

14. How do I reset my password if I forget it?
On the MCL web sign-in page use Forgot password, enter the email address registered for your account, and
follow the email reset link. Create a password that meets the company policy. If you do not receive the email
or no reset option is shown in the app, ask your company MCL administrator to verify the account email and
reset access.

18. How do I add a new user from my company to MCL?
An administrator opens the web administration area (typically Companies/Users), creates or invites the user
with their name and email, assigns the user to the company, chooses the role, and assigns the relevant
markets/departments. The new user then signs in and synchronizes the app. The exact menu and approval
process may be controlled by the company.

19. Can I change the app language (for example, to Spanish)?
Yes, MCL supports localized labels including Spanish, English and German. Use the language option in the
app/profile/settings if your version exposes it; otherwise the language can follow the user/profile or device
configuration. Restart or refresh the app after changing language. An administrator can help if the setting is not
available to your role.
15. Can I make a checklist repeat automatically (for example, a daily fridge temperature check

every morning)?
Yes. A user with Checklist Wizard/configuration permission can create a recurring checklist, set its periodicity
and weekday/time-related rules, assign the target markets/departments and roles, and save it. Example:
configure the fridge-temperature checklist as daily, assign it to the relevant department and responsible store
role, then it appears as scheduled work.
23. How does the Checklist Wizard work, step by step? Who in the company uses it to create

checklists?
The Checklist Wizard is the web configuration tool for building and publishing checklists. It is normally used by
company administrators, quality managers or other users granted checklist-management permission.
14. Open Checklists > Checklist Wizard and choose Add (or copy an existing checklist).
15. Enter the general setup: name, recurring/periodicity settings, signature requirement and any relevant tags
or groups.
16. Add departments and decide whether users may select a department.
17. Add questions, choose each question type and configure options, sequence, evidence/sensor settings and
required behavior.
18. Assign the roles and markets that may run the checklist; configure notifications/email rules if required.
19. Preview the checklist, verify the assignments and complete/save it.
20. Synchronize a test device and run a test inspection before production use.
Quick troubleshooting
•
Missing checklist or task: refresh after reconnecting; then confirm your market, department and role
assignment with an administrator.
•
Cannot attach evidence: verify that the question/task permits evidence and grant Camera/Photos
permissions in the phone settings.
•
Cannot see a report/dashboard: this is usually a role/market visibility permission issue.

MCL User Guide | Internal training reference
•
Old data after refresh: do not delete the app if offline work is pending; escalate with the device, user,
market and approximate time of the issue.
Source basis: MCL mobile and web source configuration, UI resources, task/checklist flows and repository test
screenshots. This guide intentionally distinguishes configurable behavior from guaranteed user permissions.

units.text:
Procedure: Typical daily routine in the app
1. Open MCL after connecting to the network.
2. Check whether today’s data has refreshed.
3. Review Tasks for due or overdue items.
4. Run the scheduled routine checklists for your store/department.
5. Record accurate answers and evidence at the point of work.
6. Submit completed checklists and complete assigned tasks.
7. Reconnect if necessary before leaving.
8. Confirm that the app has synchronized.
9. Resolve any failed uploads or pending items.

3. Assign the target markets/departments and roles.
4. Save the checklist.

units.text:
Procedure: How to use the Checklist Wizard step by step
1. Open Checklists > Checklist Wizard and choose Add (or copy an existing checklist).
2. Enter the general setup: name, recurring/periodicity settings, signature requirement and any relevant tags or groups.
3. Add departments and decide whether users may select a department.
4. Add questions, choose each question type and configure options, sequence, evidence/sensor settings and required behavior.
5. Assign the roles and markets that may run the checklist; configure notifications/email rules if required.
6. Preview the checklist, verify the assignments and complete/save it.
7. Synchronize a test device and run a test inspection before production use.

units.text:
Procedure: Create a checklist
1. On the Checklists page click 'New checklist' to open the editor.
2. Step 1 General information: enter the Checklist name and a General email address, and turn on Signature required or Allow department selection if you need them.
3. Step 2 Schedule and availability: set the Periodicity (for example Weekly), the Execution day, the Available from and to dates, the Time from and to, and Count current period if it should count now.
4. Step 3 Access and scope: select the Roles that run it, the Departments it applies to, and any Tags.
5. Step 4 Questions and order: after at least one department is chosen, add questions by department and drag them into the order you want.
6. Step 5 Notifications (optional): after roles are chosen, enable the roles that should be notified about executions.
7. Step 6 Preview: review the whole checklist, then 'Save draft' to keep it as a draft or 'Save and activate' to make it live. All sections are saved together in one operation. 'Ask AI Assistant' can prepare a draft for you to review first.

units.text:
Procedure: Create a task
1. On the Tasks page, click the blue New task button at the top right.
2. In the window, type a Description and choose one or more Markets (use All available markets or My markets to fill the list quickly).
3. Set the Start date and Due date. Optionally attach up to three images or a PDF, and tick Evidence required if the task must be completed with proof.
4. Click Save task to create it.

Screen: Users (web platform). Menu: Users & roles.
Users & roles is in the left menu (company administrators); the Users page is headed 'User management'. It manages accounts, roles and market/department access. Counters show Total users, Active users, Company administrators and Assignments. The table lists Full name, Email, Role, Language, Markets, Departments and Status, with Edit per row and a Search box. Roles live on the sibling Roles page. Note: you can edit, lock or remove users here, but creating a brand-new user needs a password and is done in MCL, not through the assistant.

Procedure: Change a user's role, markets or status
1. On the Users page, find the person and click Edit on their row.
2. Change their role, markets, departments, language, or lock/unlock the account, then save.
